$comment: Library configuration — single source of truth for all scripts. Copy as <library-root>/config.json. Scripts read ONLY this file; users edit keywords/sources here, never the scripts.
name: my-kb
$comment_type: intel | import | data  — the library SHAPE. Adjudication shapes (intel/import) use Bronze/Silver/Gold; data uses Fact/Derived/Conclusion. See references/medallion.md. A composite library may use an array, e.g. ["intel","data"]; the first entry is the primary shape.
$comment_language: language for generated notes/briefs (e.g. en, zh)
$comment_cadence: daily | weekly | manual — informational; actual scheduling is registered separately by the user

demand_tracking.$comment: keeper logs out-of-library queries; daily self-check surfaces a demand board; propose (not auto-add) a topic once it recurs past propose_threshold. Growth always needs owner approval.

paths.$comment: outputs/ is where things the owner asked for land — a report, an export, a rendered page. They are products of the library, not tiers of it, so they do not belong in notes/ or briefs/. Declared here so the next session can find them; created on first use, not at scaffold. Deliberately NOT indexed by index_db.py (same reason _pipeline isn't): a rendered report is a copy of knowledge, and indexing it would return the same claim twice.

$intake.$comment: Intake Gate evidence (setup/INTERVIEW.md): who decided each setup choice. decided_by is one of user-typed | user-selected | default-accepted. 'agent-inferred' is never allowed — if a field would be that, go back and ask. default-accepted is only permitted on cadence/threshold/keeper, and only if you actually stated the default AND its effect. Free text YOU drafted is default-accepted even when the user approved it — it only becomes user-typed if they rewrote it in their own words.

domain.value: what this library is for, in the user's words

$comment_intake_required: Which decisions must be on record depends on the library's SHAPE: intel needs all seven above; import needs shape/domain/categories/mode/keeper (setup/IMPORT.md); data needs shape/domain/sources/cadence/keeper — no topics, no threshold. `pipeline.py selftest` checks this. A library built before the record existed declares that honestly instead of inventing one: "$intake": { "$unrecorded": "<why>" } — it passes, and says so on every run.

built_with.$comment: How this library was actually built. toolkit_version below records the version of the TEMPLATE this file was copied from, which is NOT necessarily the version of the spec the building agent followed — one real library carries a config a version ahead of the cached skill that built it, and nothing on disk showed the difference. skill_source is the field that matters: a version number looks the same whether or not it is true, but 'a local cached copy' tells you the version is unverifiable. Say where you READ the skill from.
built_with.$comment_skill_version: a DECLARED value — the agent's own account of which spec it followed. Nothing can check it; do not treat it as evidence.
built_with.$comment_scripts_version: PASTE this from `python scripts/pipeline.py stats` — do not type it. selftest compares it against the scripts actually present, so a typed guess shows up as a mismatch.

$comment_toolkit_version: the version of the CONFIG TEMPLATE this file came from. For what the build actually ran on, see built_with.
